beats.text: One of these shapes is called Bouba. The other is Kiki. Which is which?
You probably said the round one is Bouba. So does almost everyone.
Researchers tested speakers of twenty-five languages and ten writing systems. Most matched them the same way.
Round sounds, round lips, round shape. Sharp sounds, sharp shape.
So language isn't completely random. Some sounds come with a shape.

sources: Koehler (1929); Ramachandran & Hubbard (2001), Journal of Consciousness Studies 8(12).

Cwiek et al. (2021). The bouba/kiki effect is robust across cultures and writing systems. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 377. 25 languages, 9 families, 10 writing systems; most speakers matched bouba-round, kiki-spiky (exceptions e.g. Romanian, Turkish, Mandarin). Via Leibniz-ZAS.
